set.body:
Outcome: establish independent acceptance gates before implementing the new curvature and branch estimators.

Scope: synthetic fixture generator/data and a test harness with explicit method-specific expected values, scaling laws, and tolerances. Cover open L contours; unequal turns; asymmetric closed polygons with varied starting vertices; straight lines, circles/arcs, constant-radius ribbons, and tapered branches. Include empty/short/repeated-point cases and supported endpoint/closure conventions. Preserve observed mlv2023 results as compatibility witnesses, not as truth for the new methods.

Acceptance contract:
- Turning measures count each real vertex once. Open L absolute total is 90 degrees; simple closed curves have signed total plus or minus 360 degrees under the declared orientation convention.
- Collinear subdivision, traversal reversal (including signed sign changes), rigid motion, and closed-contour cyclic reindexing preserve the appropriate quantities within justified floating-point tolerances.
- Uniform scaling obeys dimensional laws; normalized/physical representations obey their separately declared invariances. Test multiple sampling densities for branch scores.
- Tracing thresholds, raster resolutions/phases, and simplification tolerances perturb geometry: test predefined sensitivity bounds and convergence, not exact equality. Include cases where topology changes and report that boundary explicitly.
- Fix independent analytical/scalar references, fixture identities, and quantitative tolerances before new-method implementation. The harness must be runnable against candidate implementations without silently skipping missing assertions.
- Store known legacy counterexamples separately. Do not introduce permanent failing/disabled package tests; activate new API assertions with implementation while retaining the precommitted acceptance contract.
set.title: Freeze analytical, invariance, and tracing-sensitivity acceptance fixtures
